subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Sexual reproduction increases genetic variation because it involves:
options: Meiosis and the fusion of gametes from two parents
questions.explain: Meiosis plus random fertilisation combine alleles from two parents, generating variation.

questions.q: Asexual reproduction produces offspring that are:
questions.explain: Asexual reproduction (e.g. by mitosis) produces clones with no genetic variation.

questions.q: Fertilisation restores the diploid chromosome number because it is the fusion of:
options: A haploid and a diploid cell
questions.explain: Each gamete is haploid; their fusion produces a diploid zygote.

questions.q: In flowering plants, the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is called:
questions.explain: Pollination precedes fertilisation, in which the male gamete fuses with the egg cell.

questions.q: An allele is:
questions.explain: Different alleles of a gene may produce different versions of a characteristic.

questions.q: An organism with two identical alleles for a gene is described as:
questions.explain: Homozygous means two identical alleles; heterozygous means two different alleles.

questions.q: The genotype of an organism is its:
questions.explain: Genotype is the alleles present; phenotype is the observable characteristics they help produce.

questions.q: In a cross between two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt × Tt), the expected phenotype ratio of tall to short is:
questions.explain: A Tt × Tt cross gives genotypes 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so 3 tall : 1 short.

questions.q: In codominance, the heterozygote shows:
questions.explain: For example, the AB blood group expresses both A and B antigens; neither allele masks the other.

questions.q: Red–green colour blindness is more common in males because the allele is:
options: Recessive and carried on the X chromosome
Dominant and on the Y chromosome
questions.explain: Males have one X, so a single recessive allele is expressed; females need two copies.

questions.q: Homeostasis is the maintenance of:
options: A stable internal environment within narrow limits
Identical gene expression in all cells
questions.explain: Homeostasis keeps variables such as temperature, blood glucose and water balance near set points.

questions.q: Blood glucose concentration is lowered by the hormone:
questions.explain: Insulin promotes glucose uptake and storage as glycogen; glucagon raises blood glucose.

questions.q: When blood glucose falls, the pancreas releases glucagon, which causes the liver to:
options: Break down glycogen and release glucose
questions.explain: Glucagon and insulin are antagonistic hormones that keep blood glucose within limits by negative feedback.

questions.q: In thermoregulation, when the body is too hot, blood vessels in the skin:
questions.explain: Vasodilation and sweating increase heat loss; vasoconstriction and shivering conserve or generate heat when cold.

questions.q: Negative feedback control of body temperature means that a rise in temperature triggers responses that:
options: Cool the body back towards the set point
questions.explain: Negative feedback opposes the change, restoring the internal set point.

questions.q: A test cross (crossing an individual of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive) is used to:
options: Determine whether the dominant-phenotype individual is homozygous or heterozygous
questions.explain: The offspring ratios reveal the unknown genotype: all dominant suggests homozygous, a 1:1 ratio suggests heterozygous.

questions.q: Meiosis is essential to sexual reproduction because without halving the chromosome number:
options: The chromosome number would double each generation
Gametes would be diploid and stable
questions.explain: Halving at meiosis, restored at fertilisation, keeps the chromosome number constant across generations.

questions.q: After a meal high in carbohydrate, you would expect blood insulin levels to:
options: Cause glucose release from the liver
questions.explain: Rising blood glucose stimulates insulin secretion, lowering glucose back towards the set point.

questions.q: The observable characteristics of an organism make up its:
questions.explain: Phenotype results from the interaction of genotype and environment.

questions.q: In a monohybrid cross, a recessive allele is expressed in the phenotype only when the organism is:
questions.explain: A recessive characteristic appears only when both alleles are recessive; one dominant allele masks it.
